title: Introduction to random number generation
recap: A pseudo-random number generator is an algorithm that produces a sequence of numbers that behaves like random numbers. Seeding it with a fixed value makes the whole sequence reproducible, which is exactly what a deterministic exercise needs.

The standard library provides engines in <random>. std::mt19937 implements the Mersenne Twister engine, and a fixed seed makes its raw output identical on every run and across standard library implementations.
objectives: Implement rawDraw from its behavioral contract.
Practice the lesson construct by writing the control flow yourself.
Handle multiple inputs and edge cases without hard-coded example answers.
warnings: The examples are not the whole test suite; implement the general behavior.
Do not edit the test drivers. Only the supplied public function signatures are fixed.
Console output and exact source tokens are not graded.
challenge: Implement rawDraw. Construct a local std::mt19937 from seed and return its draw at zero-based drawIndex. Index 0 is the first raw engine output. Return 0 for a negative index. Every function call starts a fresh engine, so identical arguments must return identical results. No distribution and no std::rand. Tested indices are at most 100.
hints: Use seed to construct a local engine on each call.
Discard drawIndex outputs, then return the next one.
The raw engine output is specified by mt19937 and requires no distribution.
